1.why: All seven screenshots show a static, uncluttered layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary blue action buttons, bold step titles, and the highlighted current item in the progress sidebar make key controls stand out.

3.why: Clear field labels, a persistent progress list, and the same help panel on every screen let the user locate the next action quickly.

4.why: The sidebar lists all six steps, password rules appear as an on-screen checklist, and each page states the immediate next action.

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or “remember me” controls appear in any screenshot.

6.why: Completed steps turn green in the progress list, but no saved credentials or other familiar personal items are displayed.

7.why: Instructions use short plain sentences and brief bullets such as “Step X of 6” and the three-line privacy summary.

8.why: No error states are shown in the screenshots, so it is impossible to confirm whether error messages explain problems and fixes.

9.why: The approved demo email helena.demo@hospital.test is shown as a concrete example, and activity logs display sample codes, though password fields lack an example value.

10.why: The flow offers only password reset plus code entry; no alternative methods such as face login are presented as choices.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary button and at most one or two secondary actions, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Green status banners after every step explicitly state outcomes such as “New password saved securely” and “Security code confirmed.”

13.why: A persistent “Help and safe sign-in” panel and “Show a short reminder” button supply tips on every step.

14.why: Back links (e.g., “Back to recovery request”) and Pause/Resume controls allow the user to retry, although dedicated error-retry messaging is not shown.

15.why: Header, progress sidebar, help panel, and activity-log regions remain identical across all seven steps.
